question: to the Commission Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Kim Van Sparrentak (Verts/ALE), Martin Hojsík (Renew), Joanna Scheuring-Wielgus (S&D), Katrin Langensiepen (Verts/ALE), Ana Miranda Paz (Verts/ALE), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Anthony Smith (The Left), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Diana Riba i Giner (Verts/ALE), Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle (Renew), Murielle Laurent (S&D), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Manon Aubry (The Left), Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Christophe Clergeau (S&D), Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Lucia Yar (Renew), Tilly Metz (Verts/ALE), Gabriela Firea (S&D), Estelle Ceulemans (S&D), Aodhán Ó Ríordáin (S&D), Anja Hazekamp (The Left), Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE), Marit Maij (S&D), Catarina Martins (The Left), Nicolae Ștefănuță (Verts/ALE), Emma Rafowicz (S&D), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Marc Angel (S&D), Lynn Boylan (The Left), Maria Guzenina (S&D), Lena Schilling (Verts/ALE), Aurore Lalucq (S&D), Cecilia Strada (S&D) Subject:

The 2026-2030 gender equality strategy, adopted by the Commission on 5 March 2026, acknowledges for the first time that menstrual and menopause poverty affect many women across the EU. In the strategy, the Commission referenced the 2022 revision of the VAT Directive, which enabled Member States to apply a reduced or zero rate to menstrual products, and proposed organising an exchange of best practices between EU Member States regarding measures to combat menstrual and menopause poverty at national level. However, VAT reduction alone does not guarantee the accessibility of menstrual products. According to estimates, in 2024 and 2025, 42 % of European women experienced period poverty at least once1. This figure highlights the limitations of current measures and raises questions about what further steps could be taken at EU and national level to address the issue more effectively. 1.

In addition to the exchange of best practices, what EU budget mechanisms does the Commission intend to mobilise to support Member States in facilitating access to menstrual products, including, for example, the European Social Fund Plus, which already supports measures targeting poverty and social exclusion?
Will the Commission issue guidance to the Member States on the eligibility of such measures under current funding programmes?
European Survey entitled ‘Règles Élémentaires’, OpinionWay Healthcare, 2025.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.10.2026) As acknowledged by the Honourable Members, the Roadmap for Women’s Rights1 and the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-20302 recognise that tackling menstrual poverty and improving access to affordable menstrual products are important for gender equality. The Strategy also notes that, on top of the 2022 revision of the VAT Directive, other measures, such as providing menstrual products free of charge or organising free distribution for specific groups, may in some cases offer a more targeted way of supporting those most in need. In this context, Member States may use European Social Fund Plus (ESF+)3 to support basic material assistance, including hygiene products, where this supports social inclusion and addresses material deprivation. As announced in the Strategy, the Commission will also fund a study on the macro- and micro-economic and societal benefits of closing the women’s health gap related to certain conditions over the life course, including menopause. Furthermore, the EU Anti-Poverty Strategy aims to tackle the causes of poverty while improving access to affordable, high-quality social and essential services. The Commission will track progress towards the reduction of poverty, strengthen monitoring, and propose new affordability indicators. The existing regulatory framework, including the ESF+, already provides possibilities for supporting measures aimed at reducing poverty and social exclusion, where such measures fall within the scope of the relevant specific objectives and national or regional programmes. The Commission will continue to provide clarification and support to Member States, where needed, in the context of programme implementation and exchanges of good practices.
1 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and

Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions ‘A Roadmap for Women's Rights’, COM(2025)97 final. 2 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic tnd Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions ‘Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2030’, COM(2026)113 final. 3 https://european-social-fund-plus.ec.europa.eu/en.
